course_description: This course will build on the foundations of the comprehensive examination of the healthy mouth and introduce the student to the practice of minimal intervention dentistry. The course will use simulated learning environments including pre-clinical laboratories to provide students with the opportunity to attain competency in the clinical skills required to provide preventive dental care and simple dental restorations. Students will also develop their clinical skills in a clinical environment and will begin seeing patients in the summer semester. The focus is the dental management of healthy adults.

course_aims: This course aims to develop a substantial and in-depth appreciation of the connection and application of science to clinical dental practice, and to develop the procedural skills required to begin clinical practice of evidence-based minimal intervention dentistry.

learning_outcomes.description: Apply knowledge of oral diseases to explain clinical observations and to solve clinical problems.
Demonstrate competence in the procedural skills required for the practice of minimal intervention dentistry.
Demonstrate an applied knowledge of dental material properties and their application to direct restorative techniques.
Appropriately select and use instrumentation and dental materials for the practice of minimal intervention dentistry.
Apply the principles of clinical communication, behaviour management and oral health education to the clinical setting.
Demonstrate professional conduct, including while working with other members of the dental team.

assessment_details.title: Assessment Item 4- Intraoral Radiography Competency
assessment_details.due_date: 7/10/2026 - 28/10/2026 Weeks 10-13 of peer clinic. Rostered groups with LA.
assessment_details.task_description: During your radiography module, you will need to demonstrate the safe competency in taking bitewings and periapical radiographs in the peer clinic setting using the Dexter manikin. This will be assessed during your rostered peer clinic sessions, where attendance is mandatory. This competency will include intraoral film holders, orientations, as well as the bisecting angle and paralleling techniques. assessment_details.title: Assessment Item 6- Local Anaesthesia Competency
assessment_details.due_date: 7/10/2026 - 28/10/2026 Weeks 10-13 of peer clinic. Rostered groups with Radiography.
assessment_details.task_description: You will need to demonstrate the safe competency in the administration of LA during your peer clinic sessions. You will need to demonstrate sound infection control practices, the mantling and dismantling of a LA syringe, and the administration of an infiltration and an inferior alveolar nerve (with lingual) block using the correct anatomical knowledge and clinical procedure. You will also need to show palatal infiltration intraoral injection points, without needing to administer the local anaesthetic for this injection. The rubric used for the marking of this assessment will be available in Blackboard. assessment_details.title: Assessment Item 7- Clinical Case-based Viva Voce
assessment_details.task_description: You will review a written case (15 minutes), then participate in a 15-minute oral examination with 2-3 examiners. The discussion will assess your understanding and application of restorative dentistry principles and material science, clinical diagnoses with reasoning, simple treatment planning, and application of evidence-based practice. Bring writing materials such as a pen and highlighter and please wear professional attire or DMD navy scrubs. No electronic devices or additional resources permitted. Further details will be provided on the course Blackboard site. This assessment task is not eligible for a re-mark as it will be assessed by two or more examiners and post-marking moderation process will be applied.
